title: PCR Instrument-assisted Acidolysis for Monosaccharide Composition Analysis of Serum Glycans
protocol: Collect leftover serum samples after their clinical tests at the hospital.
Divide each serum sample into three aliquots in 1.5 mL EP tubes and store at -80°C.
Thaw serum samples on ice.
Transfer 5 μL of serum sample into a PCR microtube.
Add 5 μL Rha (1 mg/mL) and 10 μL HCl (6M) to each PCR microtube.
Vortex the mixture for 5 seconds and centrifuge for another 10 seconds.
Run acidolysis program on a PCR instrument for 10 minutes.
Add 20 μL NaOH (3M) and 20 μL PMP (0.5M) to each sample microtube.
Vortex the mixture for 5 seconds and centrifuge for another 10 seconds.
Run the derivatization program on a PCR instrument for 50 minutes.
Add 20 μL HAc-NH4Ac buffer to each sample tube.
Vortex for 5 s and centrifuge for another 10 s.
Add 100 μL CHCl3 into each sample tube, and shake upside down for 10 times.
Centrifuge for 10 s and remove the lower layer.
Repeat the addition of 100 μL CHCl3, shaking, and centrifugation twice.
Centrifuge for 15 min at 13,000 g/min and transfer supernatant to HPLC vials.
Dilute the stock solution of GalN, GlcA, Xyl, and Fuc to 1.25 mg/mL.
Mix the 10 monosaccharide standards together and dilute twice.
Adjust the pH of each standard mixture with 20 μL 0.2 M NaOH to reach 12-13.
Add 20 μL 0.5 M PMP for monoscharide labeling as described in Steps 8 to 11.
Assure that the LC is working appropriately according to the manufacturers’ recommendations or the standard operating procedure (SOP) of the respective laboratory.
Set up the HPLC system to separate PMP-labeled monosaccharides as described under EQUIPMENT SETUP.
